title: [Spike] Isolate what actually dominates the 500k seed-corpus run
summary: `benchmarks/seed_corpus.py` writes row-by-row with a 500-row checkpoint flush, and per EPIC-25 every vector is inlined as a SQL string literal. Measure where the time goes before committing to a `db2 LOAD` rewrite.
description:
`benchmarks/seed_corpus.py` (415 lines) drives inserts through the SDK with `_CHECKPOINT_BATCH = 500` controlling checkpoint flushes. Per the EPIC-25 audit, vectors cannot be parameter-bound on this Db2 version (`SQL0901N`) and are inlined via `CAST('{vec}' AS VECTOR(...))`, and metadata filter values are inlined too because `JSON_VALUE(col,path) = ?` segfaults the ibm_db C extension. So every row is a distinct, unprepared, fully-logged statement.

This is the suspected dominant cost in `benchmark-scale` (500k rows) and a meaningful one in `benchmark-nightly` (50k default). It is also almost certainly why the `LOGFILSIZ 4096 LOGPRIMARY 30 LOGSECOND 64` expansion exists in `setup-db2` at all.

But "suspected" is doing real work in that sentence — the cost could equally be embedding generation, Python-side content synthesis in `_generate_content`, or the per-row `random.Random` construction in `_make_row_rng`. A `db2 LOAD` rewrite is a multi-day change and shouldn't be started on a guess.

Work:

- Confirm whether `db2 LOAD` can even accept the vector column format — it bypasses the SQL layer, so `CAST(... AS VECTOR(...))` is not available and the column must be loadable from a delimited or IXF representation. **Test this before anything else: if it can't, the LOAD path is dead and the batching interventions below become the whole answer.**
- Profile a 50k seed run against containerised Db2, split into: content/metadata generation, embedding, SQL statement construction, and Db2 execution time.
- Measure how execution time scales from 1k → 50k, and whether it is linear or degrades (index maintenance, log pressure).
- Test three cheap interventions in isolation and measure each: (a) multi-row `VALUES` batching, (b) larger commit batches, (c) dropping the vector index before the load and rebuilding after.
- Check whether the checkpoint/resume machinery (`_load_checkpoint`/`_save_checkpoint`) is still needed once seeding is fast, or whether a simpler re-run is acceptable.

comments.author: implementation
comments.text: Spike preparation complete. Per-phase profiling instrumentation added to benchmarks/seed_corpus.py behind the CIW10_PROFILE=1 env var. When enabled, it prints a breakdown table to stderr at the end of the run showing time spent in content+metadata generation, embedding, and db write phases with ms/row and percentage. To run: CIW10_PROFILE=1 python benchmarks/seed_corpus.py --size 50k --seed 42. First check before profiling: does db2 LOAD accept the vector column format? Test with: docker exec <db2-container> su - db2inst1 -c 'db2 LOAD FROM /tmp/test.del OF DEL INSERT INTO test_vectors' where test_vectors has a VECTOR column. If the VECTOR type is not loadable from DEL/IXF format, close CIW-11 and pivot to multi-row VALUES batching (option 1). Note: Phase-1 changes (CIW-2..CIW-7) do not materially affect seeding time — the SQL bottleneck is unchanged.
